source.title: EMP: Enhance Memory in Data Pruning
source.authors: Jin-Ying Xiao; Ping Li; Jie Nie; Bing Ji; Sha-Sha Li; Xiao-Dong Liu; Jun Ma; Qing-Bo Wu; Jie Yu

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper and appendices; some figures and tables are flattened or represented only by plots.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how data-pruning and memory-scoring methods affect training fit and held-out performance, using experiments rather than the claim versions’ specified interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper tests dynamic data pruning and its memory term, not random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples as defined in the versions. Its own generalization experiments and pruning results are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates dynamic data pruning, not any specified claim version. Its memory scores are predictive entropy or contrastive representation losses, rather than V8's label-memorization influence. Its interpolation analysis does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap rankings. Partial label corruption supplies no V1 test of random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that adding a memory term counters insufficient sample memory under high pruning rates and improves pruning performance across image classification, natural language understanding and model pre-training. These are comparisons with pruning methods, not a demonstration that pruning consistently matches full-data training.
record.recipe_differences: Dynamic dataset pruning with a memory-augmented scoring function; not the interventions or measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning ratio; dataset; supervised versus self-supervised task; memory-term construction; β; annealing; class-balance enforcement. The authors report EMP is less effective at low pruning rates, and at higher β performance declines.

fits_no_version.finding: EMP reports competitive held-out performance across supervised classification, GLUE fine-tuning and SimCLR pre-training. Its accuracy can remain below the unpruned baseline, particularly at high pruning ratios.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memory-augmented dynamic pruning can outperform alternative pruning methods in the tested workloads, especially at high pruning ratios.

fits_no_version.finding: Enforcing equal class proportions reduces CIFAR-10 accuracy from 95.23 to 94.88 and CIFAR-100 accuracy from 79.44 to 72.21 at 50% pruning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Enforced class balance can reduce EMP's performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report lower loss and a flatter profile near the trained endpoint for EMP along the initial-to-final parameter direction, with leading accuracy along that path.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EMP has a favorable loss and accuracy profile along the particular interpolation direction examined.

record.problems: Several key generalization-analysis values are available only in figures. Table 2 does not state the metric in its displayed table. Experiments are run five times and averaged, but uncertainty is reported only for some results. The study evaluates pruning methods rather than the claim versions’ specified settings.
record.rows_left_out: Not all comparator rows from Tables 1–4 are included, nor all GLUE task-by-pruning-ratio cells. They were omitted to keep the extraction focused on EMP’s reported outcomes; comparator rankings are summarized by the authors in text. Figure-only plot values beyond the described interpolation result were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy. The 20% label-noise experiment does not establish these comparisons.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under controlled tuning, including broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, small-data and excessive-dropout regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of examples ranked by their inclusion's effect on predicting their own labels, compared with equally many random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. Citations to random-label fitting and memorization's long-tail role do not constitute new tests. No omitted result in the supplied text measures a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons and optimizer tuning.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout comparisons, including small training sets or excessive dropout.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples identified by memorization influence and comparing with random removals.

relation.reason: The paper discusses memorization, long-tail learning, and flat minima, but its results measure different constructs from the specified claim versions.

tranche.reason: EMP evaluates dynamic pruning using predictive entropy or contrastive representation losses. It tests none of V1–V8; its interpolation analysis does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap ranking.

source_check.notes: All rows describe EMP method-performance comparisons or diagnostics and should remain excluded from claim evidence. Supervised CIFAR training includes final full-data annealing; Table 1 does not substantiate the authors' claim of matching or exceeding the unpruned CIFAR100 baseline.
